- [x] **T-170** Memory is LOOKUP by default and INJECTION only on a deterministic match against the act; fix the WRITE side first, so every stored lesson carries the key (command pattern, path or error string) that would have caught the mistake (session 174) — Session 78, planner's recommendation, recorded at Aaron's request ('capture your recommendation about the fix'). NOT A RULING; Aaron has not decided it. THE SPLIT, by one question: does the agent know it needs something? (a) YES: LOOKUP. ob_recall is called with trigger 'explicit' when the agent asks. Evidence: Loop 10 measured session-start injection at p=0.688 once topic-matched, while ranking earned its keep at p=0.035; CLAUDE.md, delivered at 100% reliability, failed to change behaviour (the upper bound); HoH gained with no memory module, using an index plus fetch-on-demand. (b) NO: LOOKUP CANNOT HELP, and this is the case the PRD's 'lessons from past mistakes are forgotten' names. G-039: the store held entry 299 and the agent made that mistake anyway, because it never knew to ask. Injection is the only mechanism for this case. HOW INJECTION KNOWS WHAT IS RELEVANT: only by deriving it from the ACT, never from the session's topic, which is what failed at session start. Three act signatures, all concrete and all present at the moment it matters: (1) command shape, which is what the Loop 16 trigger does; (2) the file being edited; (3) ERROR TEXT, probably the highest-value one, since an error is exactly when an agent is about to take a known-wrong path, and error strings match precisely. Precision only, silent below the floor, as the trigger already works. THE BOTTLENECK IS THE WRITE SIDE, NOT RETRIEVAL: injection can only match an entry that carries a machine-matchable key. G-017 measured 86% of ACTION lines as prose that names no file or command, so those entries can never be injected precisely whatever the matcher does. QA's entry 615 is the same finding from the other side: two costly Loop 16 errors were in the store and unreachable. THE FIX, IN ORDER: (i) at store time (/end A12, ob_store), a lesson must carry the key that would have caught it: a command pattern, a path glob or an error signature. An entry without one is lookup-only by construction, and that is reported, not hidden; (ii) extend the trigger past Bash command shape to file-edit and tool-error events, keyed on those fields rather than on a hand-maintained element table (T-162); (iii) keep session-start injection OFF (Loop 10 C2). STILL UNPROVEN, stated so nobody builds on it as settled: four injections, all entry 299, all apt, none changed behaviour, because the practice was already loaded every time. The discriminating observation is an injection on a mistake the agent has NOT already internalised; the trigger_fires table is the instrument. Relates to G-017, G-026, G-039, T-159, T-162. —  — s171 planner census (live store, read-only, 2026-10-14): trigger_fires since 09-21 holds 40,558 fires: 22,091 not-asked, 17,328 silent, 1,139 injected, and EVERY injection is entry 299. The trigger reaches one lesson out of 708 live entries. A loose regex finds 456 entries that MENTION a command, path or error string (a mention is not a key) and 252 that mention none. - [x] **T-174** Win32 job-object launcher so the role's whole process tree is killed on a NORMAL exit too (R22's named limit on Windows) (session 174) — Session 78, from rulings-4 (R22 narrowed to option (b) on the developer's costing). Node has no job-object API. taskkill /T walks from a LIVE root, so after a role exits normally its orphans are unreachable, and descendant PID lists (WMI/CIM) are racy against PID reuse and were ruled out. Candidate A therefore kills the process group on POSIX on every exit path, and on win32 states in every iteration record that normal-exit tree-kill is unavailable. THE FIX, the developer's estimate: a small C# launcher compiled at runtime with PowerShell Add-Type. It calls CreateJobObject with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, creates the role process SUSPENDED, assigns it to the job, resumes it, relays the exit code and stdio (the prompt on stdin, the tails of stdout and stderr), and calls TerminateJobObject on the runtime's command. About 150-250 lines, plus 0.5-1.5s of PowerShell startup per stage. MUST FAIL CLOSED: Add-Type unavailable (constrained language mode) or AV interference refuses the loop and never falls back to an unkilled tree. PowerShell is a shell binary, so it may interpret only the runtime's fixed script and must pass the role's argv as data, never through a command line. CI is Linux, so only a Windows machine tests it; the row needs a Windows runner or states that limit. Residual it closes: R20's compare-then-call race on the generated config file, on the normal-exit path on Windows. — s174 10-26 CLOSED as superseded (Aaron at the planner's desk, transcript 0bbb03c4: 'Close it'). Developer work runs as QA PC job-runner claude -p runs, bounded by the runner. The normal-exit tree-kill limit stays stated in the harness records; re-open if the harness drives roles on Windows again.

- [x] **T-168** 'Run the full suite alone' must become a check: assert peer idleness before the run and refuse or flag when a peer is busy (session 173) — Opened session 77 on Aaron's ruling. THE RULE NAMES A CONDITION NO SEAT COULD VERIFY. 'Run the full suite alone at every candidate' has been in briefs since Loop 16 and every seat believed it was following it; the QA seat's slice-three baseline was run 'alone' while the planner was demonstrably active mid-run (a rulings message arrived during it) and the developer was working G-045, and it went red. A seat that believes it ran alone has an instrument that cannot tell 'nothing else was running' from 'I did not look' - G-044's class, in the one rule meant to guard the measurement. PROJECT DOCTRINE SETTLES THE FIX: a rule someone has to remember is an intention; a check is a rule. THE CHECK IS NOW POSSIBLE AND WAS DONE BY HAND TONIGHT: ListAgents lists every peer session on the machine with a busy/idle state, and calling it immediately before the suite is what made V-076's measurement mean anything. Without it the clean idle run would have been one more unlabelled data point in a table of eleven. SHAPE: before a full-suite run at a candidate, the seat calls ListAgents; if any peer is busy it REFUSES or flags loudly in the report, and either way the peer states at run time are recorded ALONGSIDE the result so a later reader can tell a contended run from a clean one. Every historical sighting lacks that field, which is why eleven measurements cannot be re-read. LIMITS TO BUILD IN, from this session's own findings: ListAgents has a REGISTRATION LAG - the developer's listing showed only the planner while the QA seat was already running - so an early or short listing is indistinguishable from a machine with nothing on it, and the check must not read an empty listing as 'idle' without a control (D-029 records this). It also cannot see non-Claude load (a build, a browser, an indexer), so it is a necessary and not a sufficient condition and must be worded as such rather than as a guarantee of idleness. RELATED: G-042 (the fault this protects the measurement of), V-076 (the controlled comparison), T-166 (another instrument that reported confidence it had not earned). --- AMENDED session 78, and Aaron ruled the policy (D-034): THE PEER SET IS NO LONGER ONLY SIA'S SEATS. The developer and QA seats agree that both surviving hypotheses are LOAD, either external (the other project's seat) or the suite's own (candidate A adds about 153s of spawning at full parallelism), and that neither is separated yet. An interactive seat can also show BUSY while its human types. POLICY (D-034): other projects' seats work normally BY DEFAULT and are RECORDED beside every SIA suite result; they pause only when a SIA seat requests a controlled rerun.
